blocks.text: Dohra:

(Dear readers) listen to the episode of volunteer Muslim recruits, Who kept themselves planted on the battlefield for the Islamic cause. Who sacrificed their lives for the cause of their Islamic faith, Together with Muslim general populace and the Islamic fundamentalists. (1)
lines: (Dear readers) listen to the episode of volunteer Muslim recruits,
Who kept themselves planted on the battlefield for the Islamic cause.
Who sacrificed their lives for the cause of their Islamic faith,
Together with Muslim general populace and the Islamic fundamentalists.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

So listen to the episode of all those Islamic volunteers, And the plight through which these fundamentalists passed. Aslam Khan4 , being sick of fighting, retreated to Lahore, As the whole of Punjab region showed defiance to his rule. (2)
lines: So listen to the episode of all those Islamic volunteers,
And the plight through which these fundamentalists passed.
Aslam Khan4 , being sick of fighting, retreated to Lahore,
As the whole of Punjab region showed defiance to his rule.

blocks.text: The Mughals failed to collect any taxes from their region, As they alleged that the Khalsa had ransacked the whole area. His troops deserted him for want of money and wages, And who pays taxes/revenue without the fear of troops? (3)
lines: The Mughals failed to collect any taxes from their region,
As they alleged that the Khalsa had ransacked the whole area.
His troops deserted him for want of money and wages,
And who pays taxes/revenue without the fear of troops?

blocks.text: Even the emperor ceases to be a friendly supporter without money, And money comes only through revenue collections from the country. First Banda Singh had harassed and robbed this region, Then the Khalsa Panth Singhs ransacked the people. (4)
lines: Even the emperor ceases to be a friendly supporter without money,
And money comes only through revenue collections from the country.
First Banda Singh had harassed and robbed this region,
Then the Khalsa Panth Singhs ransacked the people.

blocks.text: As the emperor did not receive the revenue from (Lahore), He dispatched the Mughal force for collecting the revenues. This contingent consisted of one thousand horse - mounted troops, Which was commanded by a couple of Pathan Muslim warriors. (5)
lines: As the emperor did not receive the revenue from (Lahore),
He dispatched the Mughal force for collecting the revenues.
This contingent consisted of one thousand horse - mounted troops,
Which was commanded by a couple of Pathan Muslim warriors.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Attaullan Khan5 and Mohabbat Khan6 were these two Pathan warriors, Who were both very handsome and muscular in their looks. They were reputed to be great soldiers, And had their residences in the city of Faridabad. (6)
lines: Attaullan Khan5 and Mohabbat Khan6 were these two Pathan warriors,
Who were both very handsome and muscular in their looks.
They were reputed to be great soldiers,
And had their residences in the city of Faridabad.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

From there (Faridabad7 )as these two warriors came to Lahore, Listen to the developments that took place there. The Muslim subjects (of the Punjab) came with a petition, With a faith that (these two warriors would listen to their woes. (7)
lines: From there (Faridabad7 )as these two warriors came to Lahore,
Listen to the developments that took place there.
The Muslim subjects (of the Punjab) came with a petition,
With a faith that (these two warriors would listen to their woes.

blocks.text: Members of the Muslim clergy and several other mendicants, Pressed the Nawab of Lahore unitedly (for a firm action). Holding an audience at the Court of the Nawab, All the United Muslims made joint efforts (to retaliate). (8)
lines: Members of the Muslim clergy and several other mendicants,
Pressed the Nawab of Lahore unitedly (for a firm action).
Holding an audience at the Court of the Nawab,
All the United Muslims made joint efforts (to retaliate).

blocks.text: Making a pretence of upholding and guarding their religious ideology, The Muslims made it their main issue for waging a war. Whosoever were destined to perish in this religious crusade, They were indoctrinated in this evil ideology (against the Khalsa Panth). (9)
lines: Making a pretence of upholding and guarding their religious ideology,
The Muslims made it their main issue for waging a war.
Whosoever were destined to perish in this religious crusade,
They were indoctrinated in this evil ideology (against the Khalsa Panth).

blocks.text: Making a proposal to Aslam Khan, they remarked, That they were prepared to reach Lahore voluntarily. They would neither ask for any provisions for their upkeep, Nor would they insist on the Nawab to accompany them on this crusade. (10)
lines: Making a proposal to Aslam Khan, they remarked,
That they were prepared to reach Lahore voluntarily.
They would neither ask for any provisions for their upkeep,
Nor would they insist on the Nawab to accompany them on this crusade.

blocks.text: Dohra:

They planted a Haidri8 (Islamic) flag with Islamic inscriptions, On the premises of a Mosque (on the city outskirts) of Lahore. They gave a call to all those who swore by Islamic ideology, To come forward and join their ranks of crusaders. (11)
lines: They planted a Haidri8 (Islamic) flag with Islamic inscriptions,
On the premises of a Mosque (on the city outskirts) of Lahore.
They gave a call to all those who swore by Islamic ideology,
To come forward and join their ranks of crusaders.

blocks.text: Sortha:

The Islamic fundamentalists, hearing this religions call, Girded up their loins and joined the crusaders' ranks. They stood expectant as if they were in for a grand feast, Little knowing that Death was actually waiting to devour them. (12)
lines: The Islamic fundamentalists, hearing this religions call,
Girded up their loins and joined the crusaders' ranks.
They stood expectant as if they were in for a grand feast,
Little knowing that Death was actually waiting to devour them.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Making such hype (in the name religious ideology). All these Islamic factions camped at Lahore. There were Mohammad Taki9 and Inayat Khan10 among them, Who planted their own flags in the open ground. (13)
lines: Making such hype (in the name religious ideology).
All these Islamic factions camped at Lahore.
There were Mohammad Taki9 and Inayat Khan10 among them,
Who planted their own flags in the open ground.

blocks.text: They got a public declaration made on their behalf, That those without any means could join their ranks. There was another business Tycoon Murtza Khan" , Who also joined this crusade in the interest of community welfare. (14)
lines: They got a public declaration made on their behalf,
That those without any means could join their ranks.
There was another business Tycoon Murtza Khan" ,
Who also joined this crusade in the interest of community welfare.

blocks.text: These crusaders were joined by Haji Beg Mughal12 , As well as Pir Mohammad13 , a slandering Muslim cleric. The Muslim Rajput Inayatullah from Traori too arrived, To put his own neck into the impending noose. (15)
lines: These crusaders were joined by Haji Beg Mughal12 ,
As well as Pir Mohammad13 , a slandering Muslim cleric.
The Muslim Rajput Inayatullah from Traori too arrived,
To put his own neck into the impending noose.

blocks.text: Dohra:

There used to be Raja Todar Mai14 (in the recent past), Who happened to be a revenue minister under emperor Akbar. Pahar Mai15 who happened to be the son of Todar Mai, Also got involved in this crusade, being a simpleton. (16)
lines: There used to be Raja Todar Mai14 (in the recent past),
Who happened to be a revenue minister under emperor Akbar.
Pahar Mai15 who happened to be the son of Todar Mai,
Also got involved in this crusade, being a simpleton.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He also falling a prey to the impending doom, Arrived to join the Islamic crusaders in their camp. He got a declaration made on his own behalf, That he would finance anyone who ran short of money. (17)
lines: He also falling a prey to the impending doom,
Arrived to join the Islamic crusaders in their camp.
He got a declaration made on his own behalf,
That he would finance anyone who ran short of money.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The horse-mounted one thousand soldiers from Delhi, They had arrived to collect revenues from Punjab. They, having lost their wits (in this malice of raging fanaticism), Were also pushed into this conflict by the presiding deity of Death. (18)
lines: The horse-mounted one thousand soldiers from Delhi,
They had arrived to collect revenues from Punjab.
They, having lost their wits (in this malice of raging fanaticism),
Were also pushed into this conflict by the presiding deity of Death.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

They offered their own canons for the Nawab's troops, As well as they made their light guns available. They also offered to provide employment to all those, Who had the guts to participate in this religious crusade. (19)
lines: They offered their own canons for the Nawab's troops,
As well as they made their light guns available.
They also offered to provide employment to all those,
Who had the guts to participate in this religious crusade.

blocks.text: A host of Islamic hordes marched towards Lahore, Swelling the ranks of those shouting "Ali, Ali" slogans, Carrying a wide variety of Islamic flags and banners, A huge crowd of Islamic populace assembled there. (20)
lines: A host of Islamic hordes marched towards Lahore,
Swelling the ranks of those shouting "Ali,
Ali" slogans,
Carrying a wide variety of Islamic flags and banners,
A huge crowd of Islamic populace assembled there.

blocks.text: The Singhs, being in extreme minority against this vast majority, Were desperately in search of a place where to take refuge. Singhs, being not worth a tiny whirlwind, against the Islamic blinding storm, Were reluctant to enter into an open conflict with Muslims. (21)
lines: The Singhs, being in extreme minority against this vast majority,
Were desperately in search of a place where to take refuge.
Singhs, being not worth a tiny whirlwind, against the Islamic blinding storm,
Were reluctant to enter into an open conflict with Muslims.

blocks.text: Singhs in minority being helpless against the Muslim majority, Would find every opportunity to avoid confrontation. Thus, Singhs, finding themselves in a dire state, Would escape to find shelter in the dense wilds. (22)
lines: Singhs in minority being helpless against the Muslim majority,
Would find every opportunity to avoid confrontation.
Thus,
Singhs, finding themselves in a dire state,
Would escape to find shelter in the dense wilds.

blocks.text: Dohra:
So the Singhs would run away to seek shelter, Wherever they could spot out a forest cover. Hiding themselves in the marshy swamp of Kahnuwan16, They managed to survive on fish and wild animals. (23)
lines: So the Singhs would run away to seek shelter,
Wherever they could spot out a forest cover.
Hiding themselves in the marshy swamp of Kahnuwan16,
They managed to survive on fish and wild animals.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

In whatever direction these Islamic hordes proceeded, They started committing oppression on the Hindu populace. Committing oppression of innocent Brahmins and their daughters, They subjected the Hindus populace to several atrocities. (24)
lines: In whatever direction these Islamic hordes proceeded,
They started committing oppression on the Hindu populace.
Committing oppression of innocent Brahmins and their daughters,
They subjected the Hindus populace to several atrocities.

blocks.text: The Islamic forces committed many atrocities on people of Majha17 , Alleging that these people have enlisted their sons in the Khalsa Panth. Accusing the Singhs of supporting their families after robbing people, The Muslims forces harassed and tortured the Hindus/(Sikhs). (25)
lines: The Islamic forces committed many atrocities on people of Majha17 ,
Alleging that these people have enlisted their sons in the Khalsa Panth.
Accusing the Singhs of supporting their families after robbing people,
The Muslims forces harassed and tortured the Hindus/(Sikhs).

blocks.text: Dohra:

The news that Mughal forces were torturing the people of Majha, Soon reached the Singhs (hiding in the marshes and wilds). They felt that it was worthless to keep alive, When their parents were being tortured at home. (26)
lines: The news that Mughal forces were torturing the people of Majha,
Soon reached the Singhs (hiding in the marshes and wilds).
They felt that it was worthless to keep alive,
When their parents were being tortured at home.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter the Singhs became alert and assertive, And started pouncing upon the Muslim troops. They kept torturing Muslims at every opportune moment day and night, And blocking their movement on the main highways. (27)
lines: Thereafter the Singhs became alert and assertive,
And started pouncing upon the Muslim troops.
They kept torturing Muslims at every opportune moment day and night,
And blocking their movement on the main highways.

blocks.text: As the Mughals killed Singhs after hunting and hounding them, The Singhs also launched retaliatory attacks on them. These retaliations made the Mughals also apprehensive, As they found it quite difficult to enter Lahore. (28)
lines: As the Mughals killed Singhs after hunting and hounding them,
The Singhs also launched retaliatory attacks on them.
These retaliations made the Mughals also apprehensive,
As they found it quite difficult to enter Lahore.

blocks.text: The Singhs also started stalking and circling round the Mughals, And slaughtered every odd Muslim whom they came across. But when the Mughals came in hot pursuit of the Singhs, The Singhs would camouflage themselves behind bushes and ferns. (29)
lines: The Singhs also started stalking and circling round the Mughals,
And slaughtered every odd Muslim whom they came across.
But when the Mughals came in hot pursuit of the Singhs,
The Singhs would camouflage themselves behind bushes and ferns.

blocks.text: The Mughal troops were scared to get into the bushes. As the Singhs would slaughter anyone who dared to enter. While the Singhs could remain in battle gear day and night, The Mughal troops preferred to relax all the time. (30)
lines: The Mughal troops were scared to get into the bushes.
As the Singhs would slaughter anyone who dared to enter.
While the Singhs could remain in battle gear day and night,
The Mughal troops preferred to relax all the time.

blocks.text: Sortha:

The Singhs made the Mughals exhausted and fatigued, Through their continuous harassment day and night. The (luxury loving) Mughals cried for their mothers, Whenever thorns pierced their flesh in the marshes. (31)
lines: The Singhs made the Mughals exhausted and fatigued,
Through their continuous harassment day and night.
The (luxury loving) Mughals cried for their mothers,
Whenever thorns pierced their flesh in the marshes.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Singhs, then, divided themselves into four contingents, Positioning one contingent in Majha and the hills each. Stationing another contingent in the vicinity of Lahore, The fourth contingent was deputed to keep stalking the Mughals. (32)
lines: The Singhs, then, divided themselves into four contingents,
Positioning one contingent in Majha and the hills each.
Stationing another contingent in the vicinity of Lahore,
The fourth contingent was deputed to keep stalking the Mughals.

blocks.text: While each contingent consisted of two hundred Singhs, One or two odd Singhs kept on joining these contingents. Whenever a single contingent got surrounded by the Mughals, Other contingents would rush immediately to its rescue. (33)
lines: While each contingent consisted of two hundred Singhs,
One or two odd Singhs kept on joining these contingents.
Whenever a single contingent got surrounded by the Mughals,
Other contingents would rush immediately to its rescue.

blocks.text: However, the events took such a turn for the worse, That the Mughals laid a siege around one of the contingents. There was a Kshtriya by the name Bhagwant18, Who was a resident of Bharatpur on the banks of the Ravi. (34)
lines: However, the events took such a turn for the worse,
That the Mughals laid a siege around one of the contingents.
There was a Kshtriya by the name Bhagwant18,
Who was a resident of Bharatpur on the banks of the Ravi.

blocks.text: He had constructed a Mansion in that village, In which a Singh contingent happened to enter. Perhaps, the Singhs wished to seek shelter from the rains, Or God knows why did they enter this Mansion. (35)
lines: He had constructed a Mansion in that village,
In which a Singh contingent happened to enter.
Perhaps, the Singhs wished to seek shelter from the rains,
Or God knows why did they enter this Mansion.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The information about the Singhs hiding in that mansion, Reached the Mughal contingent of one thousand horse-mounted troops. As this contingent laid a siege to the Mansion immediately, More reinforcements arrived in support of this contingent. (36)
lines: The information about the Singhs hiding in that mansion,
Reached the Mughal contingent of one thousand horse-mounted troops.
As this contingent laid a siege to the Mansion immediately,
More reinforcements arrived in support of this contingent.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Singhs inside the mansion came under a siege, Those out on errands were killed by the Mughal troops. Making Pickets all around the Mansion under siege, They raised mud walls and large obstructions around these. (37)
lines: As the Singhs inside the mansion came under a siege,
Those out on errands were killed by the Mughal troops.
Making Pickets all around the Mansion under siege,
They raised mud walls and large obstructions around these.

blocks.text: By positioning canons and light guns on these pickets, They caused a lot of harassment to the Singhs. Singhs had no means to replenish their stores, Whatever provisions they had had been consumed. (38)
lines: By positioning canons and light guns on these pickets,
They caused a lot of harassment to the Singhs.
Singhs had no means to replenish their stores,
Whatever provisions they had had been consumed.

blocks.text: Singhs, thus getting extremely desperate and helpless, Were almost on the verge of death without provisions. The Khalsa Panth itself was not in a position to assist, As its Singhs themselves were trying to survive somehow. (39)
lines: Singhs, thus getting extremely desperate and helpless,
Were almost on the verge of death without provisions.
The Khalsa Panth itself was not in a position to assist,
As its Singhs themselves were trying to survive somehow.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Ascertaining that the Singhs had exhausted and fatigued, The Mughals launched an attack from all the sides. Since there was neither any moat nor wall around the mansion, The Singhs felt themselves in a very tight spot. (40)
lines: Ascertaining that the Singhs had exhausted and fatigued,
The Mughals launched an attack from all the sides.
Since there was neither any moat nor wall around the mansion,
The Singhs felt themselves in a very tight spot.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Mughal troops climbed up the mansion walls, The Singhs kept on chopping of their hands from above. As more and more reinforcements kept arriving, The Mughals queered the pitch of war for the Singhs. (41)
lines: As the Mughal troops climbed up the mansion walls,
The Singhs kept on chopping of their hands from above.
As more and more reinforcements kept arriving,
The Mughals queered the pitch of war for the Singhs.

blocks.text: As the Mughals fired balls of fire from their mounted canons, There were cries of death and destruction all around. The Mughals shouted that since the Singhs had come into their grip, They would never be able to escape this time. (42)
lines: As the Mughals fired balls of fire from their mounted canons,
There were cries of death and destruction all around.
The Mughals shouted that since the Singhs had come into their grip,
They would never be able to escape this time.

blocks.text: The Singhs declared that they would not die in vain, As they would kill the Mughals as well before their death. Then Satguru sent a providential help from the heavens, As a fierce blinding storm and heavy rain set in. (43)
lines: The Singhs declared that they would not die in vain,
As they would kill the Mughals as well before their death.
Then Satguru sent a providential help from the heavens,
As a fierce blinding storm and heavy rain set in.

blocks.text: As the Mughal cannons, guns and muskets got moistened, The Singhs ran out wielding swords, arrows and shields. Since the Singhs were scarcely scared of facing death, They killed a large number of Mughals with their swords. (44)
lines: As the Mughal cannons, guns and muskets got moistened,
The Singhs ran out wielding swords, arrows and shields.
Since the Singhs were scarcely scared of facing death,
They killed a large number of Mughals with their swords.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Mughals, turning their backs, took to their heels, And took shelter in the designated barracks. Taking a full advantage of this rare opportunity, Singhs rushed and entered the marshes and wilds. (45)
lines: The Mughals, turning their backs, took to their heels,
And took shelter in the designated barracks.
Taking a full advantage of this rare opportunity,
Singhs rushed and entered the marshes and wilds.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

While the Mughals considered it a great victory, The Singhs declared that they had survived this invasion. While the Mughals started marching towards Lahore, The Singhs wished to search for a new place for survival. (46)
lines: While the Mughals considered it a great victory,
The Singhs declared that they had survived this invasion.
While the Mughals started marching towards Lahore,
The Singhs wished to search for a new place for survival.

blocks.text: The Mughal troops took great pride in the fact, That they had made the Singhs flee from the field. The Khalsa Panth which had routed the great Mughals, They had now killed the great warriors of that Panth. (47)
lines: The Mughal troops took great pride in the fact,
That they had made the Singhs flee from the field.
The Khalsa Panth which had routed the great Mughals,
They had now killed the great warriors of that Panth.

blocks.text: The Mughal troops put up a camp at Bhilowal" , Considering it a suitable site for their camping. Finding an old fort lying vacant at that place, The one thousand Pathan contingent took shelter inside it. (48)
lines: The Mughal troops put up a camp at Bhilowal" ,
Considering it a suitable site for their camping.
Finding an old fort lying vacant at that place,
The one thousand Pathan contingent took shelter inside it.

blocks.text: The Muslim volunteers also put up a camp on one side, Spotting out a vantage point in that area. They thought of entering their homes on some auspicious day, After consulting the Muslim clerics about the happy occasion. (49)
lines: The Muslim volunteers also put up a camp on one side,
Spotting out a vantage point in that area.
They thought of entering their homes on some auspicious day,
After consulting the Muslim clerics about the happy occasion.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Mughal forces stationed themselves near Lahore, After ruling out all fears of any kind of attack. But as they were destined to be buried in graves there, How could they escape from the place of their doom? (50)
lines: The Mughal forces stationed themselves near Lahore,
After ruling out all fears of any kind of attack.
But as they were destined to be buried in graves there,
How could they escape from the place of their doom?

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As their fate had willed to bury them there, (Dear readers) see what had destiny in store for them. Since whatever is destined is bound to happen, The destiny had willed to grant victory to the Khalsa Panth. (51)
lines: As their fate had willed to bury them there,
(Dear readers) see what had destiny in store for them.
Since whatever is destined is bound to happen,
The destiny had willed to grant victory to the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Singhs entered the sanctuary of the wilds, They regretted the loss of opportunity of beating the Mughals, They felt like a tiger having missed its prey, And feeling a great regret at the loss of opportunity. (52)
lines: As the Singhs entered the sanctuary of the wilds,
They regretted the loss of opportunity of beating the Mughals,
They felt like a tiger having missed its prey,
And feeling a great regret at the loss of opportunity.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

(Dear readers), listen to the Singhs' sense of regret and rage, And the way the Singh displayed their manhood once again. As the Singhs were regretting their flight from the field, It was raining and a stromy wind was blowing. (53)
lines: (Dear readers), listen to the Singhs' sense of regret and rage,
And the way the Singh displayed their manhood once again.
As the Singhs were regretting their flight from the field,
It was raining and a stromy wind was blowing.

blocks.text: Had they given a chase to the fleeing Mughal troops, They would have massacred them there and then. They had always been claiming themselves as great warriors, Who never behaved cowardly in a moment of crisis. (54)
lines: Had they given a chase to the fleeing Mughal troops,
They would have massacred them there and then.
They had always been claiming themselves as great warriors,
Who never behaved cowardly in a moment of crisis.

blocks.text: As they were still confabulating over what had happened, A contingent of a few Singhs arrived there instantly. This had always been the tradition in the Khalsa Panth, That when ten Singhs died, twenty more arrived there. (55)
lines: As they were still confabulating over what had happened,
A contingent of a few Singhs arrived there instantly.
This had always been the tradition in the Khalsa Panth,
That when ten Singhs died, twenty more arrived there.

blocks.text: As these Singhs had heard the sound of gunfire at that fort, They had rushed there to assist their brethren. As their strength increased to one thousand there, The Singhs were filled with new vigour for a new attempt. (56)
lines: As these Singhs had heard the sound of gunfire at that fort,
They had rushed there to assist their brethren.
As their strength increased to one thousand there,
The Singhs were filled with new vigour for a new attempt.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then a Singh arrived there with a fresh information, That the Mughals were still not keen to enter Lahore. They, too, were thinking of launching an attack on the Singhs, Although they might attack (with gunfire) from a distance. (57)
lines: Then a Singh arrived there with a fresh information,
That the Mughals were still not keen to enter Lahore.
They, too, were thinking of launching an attack on the Singhs,
Although they might attack (with gunfire) from a distance.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Hearing this news, the Khalsa Singhs went into a rage, As if a flint-stone was hit with the force of gun's trigger. The Singhs then resolved to make preparations for an attack, Either to eliminate the Mughals or sacrifice their own lives. (58)
lines: Hearing this news, the Khalsa Singhs went into a rage,
As if a flint-stone was hit with the force of gun's trigger.
The Singhs then resolved to make preparations for an attack,
Either to eliminate the Mughals or sacrifice their own lives.

blocks.text: Girding up their loins they rushed to launch an attack, As they had no horses to harness and mount. Since they had no baggage or equipment to be carried, They just rushed after invoking blessings of Guru Gobind Singh. (59)
lines: Girding up their loins they rushed to launch an attack,
As they had no horses to harness and mount.
Since they had no baggage or equipment to be carried,
They just rushed after invoking blessings of Guru Gobind Singh.

blocks.text: They rushed on foot with the speed of horses, Without stopping over hills or swamps on the way. Running along the river bed, they arrived near Lahore, And surveyed the positions of contingents of Mughal troops. (60)
lines: They rushed on foot with the speed of horses,
Without stopping over hills or swamps on the way.
Running along the river bed, they arrived near Lahore,
And surveyed the positions of contingents of Mughal troops.

blocks.text: Now (dear readers) listen to the account of Mughals forces, Who were proceeding towards the city of Lahore. With the beat of drums and play on pipes signifying victory, They were firing shots from canons and light guns. (61)
lines: Now (dear readers) listen to the account of Mughals forces,
Who were proceeding towards the city of Lahore.
With the beat of drums and play on pipes signifying victory,
They were firing shots from canons and light guns.

blocks.text: Dohra:

After fixing an auspicious day for their entry into Lahore, They had been camping at the place of Bhilowal, Their trained troops had entered into the fort, As they liked their forts (from security point of view). (62)
lines: After fixing an auspicious day for their entry into Lahore,
They had been camping at the place of Bhilowal,
Their trained troops had entered into the fort,
As they liked their forts (from security point of view).

blocks.text: As their destined death was looming large over them, They had delayed their departure for Lahore. The Singhs suddenly pounced upon them unawares, As a flying hawk pounces upon the prey from the skies. (63)
lines: As their destined death was looming large over them,
They had delayed their departure for Lahore.
The Singhs suddenly pounced upon them unawares,
As a flying hawk pounces upon the prey from the skies.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Singhs made a sudden rush into the fort, The Mughals rushed out without putting any resistance, While a few had gone out on a hunting spree, A few others had gone on a visit to the village. (64)
lines: As the Singhs made a sudden rush into the fort,
The Mughals rushed out without putting any resistance,
While a few had gone out on a hunting spree,
A few others had gone on a visit to the village.

blocks.text: While a few were making ablutions before a morning prayer, A few others were prostrating while reciting prayers. Their heavy canons and light guns remained lying unused, As the bullocks for pulling the gun carriages were out for grazing (65)
lines: While a few were making ablutions before a morning prayer,
A few others were prostrating while reciting prayers.
Their heavy canons and light guns remained lying unused,
As the bullocks for pulling the gun carriages were out for grazing

blocks.text: . The horses which were standing harnessed and saddled, The Singhs jumped and mounted those horses instantly. Mounting those horses, the Singh started attacking the enemy, And killing them by marching ahead of each other. (66)
lines: The horses which were standing harnessed and saddled,
The Singhs jumped and mounted those horses instantly.
Mounting those horses, the Singh started attacking the enemy,
And killing them by marching ahead of each other.

blocks.text: The Singhs killed the Mughals after a thorough search, As it was an ideological war between the Mughals and the Khalsa Panth. As the Singhs sliced each Mughal's soldier into one to four pieces, They displayed rare acts of valour in this field of battle. (67)
lines: The Singhs killed the Mughals after a thorough search,
As it was an ideological war between the Mughals and the Khalsa Panth.
As the Singhs sliced each Mughal's soldier into one to four pieces,
They displayed rare acts of valour in this field of battle.

blocks.text: Dohra:

There were others who rushed to assist their colleagues, They were the Pathans who had come out of the fort. The Khalsa Singhs shreded them as well into pieces, Who dared to confront the Singhs in the battlefield. (68)
lines: There were others who rushed to assist their colleagues,
They were the Pathans who had come out of the fort.
The Khalsa Singhs shreded them as well into pieces,
Who dared to confront the Singhs in the battlefield.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

There was one (Ataula Khan) Naki Rajput from Tarawari, Who observed the Muslim troops caught in a cleft stick, He, climbing up a high dome, shouted loudly to his soldiers, That they must flee and take refugee in the village. (69)
lines: There was one (Ataula Khan) Naki Rajput from Tarawari,
Who observed the Muslim troops caught in a cleft stick,
He, climbing up a high dome, shouted loudly to his soldiers,
That they must flee and take refugee in the village.

blocks.text: Thus, those alone who entered the village, survived, Those standing out were butchered by the Singhs. While the Lahore troops were robbed and killed by the Singhs, Only those survived who managed to enter the village. (70)
lines: Thus, those alone who entered the village, survived,
Those standing out were butchered by the Singhs.
While the Lahore troops were robbed and killed by the Singhs,
Only those survived who managed to enter the village.

blocks.text: Murtaza Khan who was a big business tycoon and financier, Was also killed along with the grandson of Raja Todar Mai. Haji Babar Beg was also killed by the Singhs, Along with several Muslim Pirs and Islamic medicants. (71)
lines: Murtaza Khan who was a big business tycoon and financier,
Was also killed along with the grandson of Raja Todar Mai.
Haji Babar Beg was also killed by the Singhs,
Along with several Muslim Pirs and Islamic medicants.

blocks.text: While several Muslim clerics, pirs and Mohammad Inayat Khan were killed, Mirza Naki alone could survive Singhs' attack, All of these had come for the sake of defending their religion, And for killing Singhs as an act of religious duty. (72)
lines: While several Muslim clerics, pirs and Mohammad Inayat Khan were killed,
Mirza Naki alone could survive Singhs' attack,
All of these had come for the sake of defending their religion,
And for killing Singhs as an act of religious duty.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Although all of them had come to kill the Singhs, But they were themselves killed in this campaign. The Singhs, having decimated the Mughal invaders, Shouted slogans of victory by reciting God's name. (73)
lines: Although all of them had come to kill the Singhs,
But they were themselves killed in this campaign.
The Singhs, having decimated the Mughal invaders,
Shouted slogans of victory by reciting God's name.

blocks.text: After robbing, plundering and beating the Mughals in war, The Singhs occupied most of the Mughal places. The Singhs were now roaming as fearlessly in Panjab, As a lion walks in a jungle freely and fearlessly. (74)
lines: After robbing, plundering and beating the Mughals in war,
The Singhs occupied most of the Mughal places.
The Singhs were now roaming as fearlessly in Panjab,
As a lion walks in a jungle freely and fearlessly.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

In this way, the Khalsa Panth eliminated the Mughal forces, As each Singh was equal in valour to one thousand. The number of Singhs who were killed in the fortress, Four times that number had reached the fortress at night. (75)
lines: In this way, the Khalsa Panth eliminated the Mughal forces,
As each Singh was equal in valour to one thousand.
The number of Singhs who were killed in the fortress,
Four times that number had reached the fortress at night.

blocks.text: When one Mughal sildier died, the others started panting for breath, As if an epidemic had struck a flock of sheep. By the time the Mughals reorganized their troops, The Singhs had disappeared along with huge war booty. (76)
lines: When one Mughal sildier died, the others started panting for breath,
As if an epidemic had struck a flock of sheep.
By the time the Mughals reorganized their troops,
The Singhs had disappeared along with huge war booty.
